pr_body:
This is an alternative API for the L2CAP receive functionality. It allows an application the receive L2CAP segments directly and manage credits explictly. The API is guarded by an experimental kconfig option.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/57485

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: Application-managed L2CAP credits
issue_context.body:
[Android ASHA] requires an initial credit count of 8. It is not possible to satisfy this requirement in Zephyr after the change in the [L2CAP credit fix]. This requirement is vital for interoperability with current software[^1].

 [^1]: The [Android implementation] does actually not enforce 8 initial credits, but uses the actual received initial credits in a calculation. This calculation does not deal well with just 1 initial credit.

[L2CAP credit fix]: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/55519

[Android ASHA]: https://source.android.com/docs/core/connect/bluetooth/asha#starting-and-stopping-an-audio-stream

[Android implementation]: https://cs.android.com/android/platform/superproject/+/refs/heads/master:packages/modules/Bluetooth/system/bta/hearing_aid/hearing_aid.cc;l=1318;drc=1e59b5eeb1336e93fb22b8f829bde5807b8b0e4e
comments:
To fix this regression, we need to make `init_credits` significant again. However, `init_credits` in its current form is an awkward interface because it specifies credits for L2CAP PDUs, but the application provides buffers for SDUs.

The Host could interpret the `init_credits` field as the number of SDU buffers the application has to give out and manage credits accordingly. Host would keep track of the number of available buffers and give out a credit when a buffer becomes available. This definition of `init_credits` would be natural for any application that does not have any guarantees from the remote.

But sometimes, the application layer has more information than the Host, and wishes to use credits a specialized fashion. So this is an opportunity define an alternative simplified API for L2CAP that presents the application directly with L2CAP PDUs and allows the application to control the credits explicitly. In the case of ASHA, the specification guarantees that no L2CAP segmentation will occur, so this is perfect. This simplified API would allow applications that have this kind of guarantee to omit compiling in code for L2CAP fragmentation. This API would also benefit applications wish to optimize throughput by making use of some known guarantees or at the cost of reliability.

Same applies for all LOG statements in this function
Do you really need the explicit typecast? I'd have thought that the type gets inferred from the type of `*ev`.
I assume that doing it this way will ensure that any other fields are set to `0`, similar to "regular" struct initialization?

It's simpler than it looks. I'm happy to explain :)

> Do you really need the explicit typecast? I'd have thought that the type gets inferred from the type of `*ev`.

This is not a declaration, so the special declaration syntax (`= {...}`) does not apply. This is simply a combined use of an object literal, assignment and pointer de-referencing. Object literals always have the form `(type){initializer-list}`.

There is no 'downwards' type inference in C. The object literal is a child-node of the assignment. The child-node does not get type information from the parent, so the object literal must know it's own type.

> I assume that doing it this way will ensure that any other fields are set to `0`, similar to "regular" struct initialization?

This is correct. As explained above, this is a normal object literal, and struct assignment is equivalent to assigning all fields of the struct type one-by-one. Struct assignment semantics are not special for object literals; it works just as well for two struct variables `obj1 = obj2;`.

I would love if there was a linter pragma "no fields omitted in initializer", but there was nothing that easy. So omitted fields are just zeroed as you say.

I think there is a slight benefit to zeroing over just not initializing, as it's deterministic and zeros are easier to spot when debugging. Seeing as there is no new language feature here, I hope we can keep this as is, but I don't have any issue changing this to scalar assignments if we prefer that. I value you input on the readability aspect of this :)
